BREAKING: Iran has weighed attacking US Military targets in Europe should President Trump escalate the war, per FT.

Details include:

1. Iranian forces have reportedly assessed striking US assets in south-eastern European countries such as Bulgaria

2. Cyprus, where a British air base was struck by a drone in March, was also among potential targets for retaliation in the event of any renewed US offensive

3. Iranian forces have also reportedly considered attacking subsea fiber-optic cables in the Strait of Hormuz in the event of an escalation

Iran is ready to expand its range of targets should the war escalate again.

BREAKING: US margin debt dropped -$85 billion in July, to $1.42 trillion, the largest monthly decline on record.

This also marks the first monthly decrease since March.

By comparison, the 2nd-biggest monthly drop was recorded in January 2022 at -$80 billion, just as the bear market started.

This all follows a +$198 billion jump in margin debt in May and June, the largest 2-month increase on record.

Despite this record decline, margin debt has still surged +$518 billion, or +58%, since the start of 2025.

Levered investors were crushed last month.

BREAKING: Hedge funds purchased US equities in every trading session last week.

In total, this marked their 2nd-largest weekly purchase over the last 12 months.

Single stocks accounted for ~70% of the total, driven primarily by long equity purchases and, to a lesser extent, short covering.

Information technology and communication services saw the strongest demand, with 8 of 11 sectors recording purchases.

Meanwhile, macro products, such as index futures and ETFs, accounted for ~30% of total demand, with short positions in US-listed ETFs reduced for the 6th consecutive week.

Hedge funds are doubling down on US equities.

BREAKING: The SEC announces new proposed rules that will create a "clear and fit-for purpose framework" for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets.

Details include:

1. The proposal follows the SEC's March 2026 interpretation clarifying how federal securities laws apply to certain crypto assets

2. The rules will address "long-standing barriers" to "capital formation and innovation" within domestic crypto asset markets

3. The proposed rules include 2 exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933 specifically tailored to certain investment contracts involving crypto assets

4. The proposed rules also include a conditional safe harbor from the term "investment contract" in the definitions of "security" in the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934

Framework for broader crypto adoption is rolling out.

Hidden AI-related commitments are skyrocketing among Big Tech companies:

The top 9 US tech firms have ~$3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments, including leases for data centers and power infrastructure that have not yet commenced, as well as purchase commitments for AI-related equipment and services.

This is roughly triple the amount that these firms report on their balance sheets in leases and long-term debt.

This also compares to ~$600 billion in CapEx reported over the last year.

Alphabet, $GOOGL, alone posted an increase of more than +800% YoY in off-balance-sheet obligations, more than 7 times its YoY increase in CapEx.

This was followed by Meta, $META, which reported an increase of more than +750% YoY in such obligations, more than 9 times the increase in CapEx over the same period.

AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest corporate investment waves in history.

The (re-arranged and improved) heat map below shows that earnings and margins continue to drive the momentum for equities, while breadth is robust and sentiment shows more enthusiasm. On the AI side, token expenditures continue to plummet (cut in half since June) while ORCL’s CDS remains near its wides. This combination suggests ongoing pressure on the frontier models as AI consumers go down-market. Chip lease rates are stable to rising, suggesting that the AI use case remains strong. Non-AI equities remain negative correlated to AI equities while the S&P equal-weighted index is un-correlated to the Mag 7. Both metrics suggest that there are plenty of places to “hide” from an AI/hyperscalers setback, even within the equity market.
